newsitem.title: USA: Natgas futures end lower ahead of holiday.
newsitem.headline: Natgas futures end lower ahead of holiday.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended lower across the board Friday, pressured by reports of a soft early September cash, but trade remained sluggish, with many out ahead of the U.S. Labor Day holiday Monday.
October slipped 4.8 cents to close at $1.859 per million British thermal units. November settled 3.1 cents lower at $2.015. Others ended down by one to three cents.

"There's no real fundamentals to push it up, but technically, it's so oversold I'd be a scale down buyer here," said one New York-based futures trader. NYMEX and KCBT will be closed Monday for the U.S. Labor Day holiday.

Traders said storm concerns ahead of the long weekend likely kept aggressive bears at bay Friday. Some said September cash may be buoyed later next week by revised forecasts for above-normal Northeast and Midwest temperatures, but most agreed there were few other factors to sustain a rally near-term.

September cash prices at the U.S. Gulf notionally fell a couple of cents Friday to the mid-$1.70s, with swing prices in the $1.60-1.70 area. Midcon pipes were steady to up slightly in the low-to-mid $1.60s.
Technically, traders pegged October support at yesterday's low of $1.85 and then at $1.82. Resistance was seen first at $1.955 and then in the $2.08-2.09 area.
The 12-month strip fell 1.2 cents to $2.021. NYMEX said 10,681 Henry Hub contracts traded, down from Thursday's revised tally of 21,624.
NYMEX Permian natgas closed two cents lower at $1.56, while deferreds settled down by one to four cents. NYMEX said 86 Permian lots changed hands, up from zero on Thursday.

On the KCBT, October finished 1.2 cents lower at $1.63, while deferreds closed steady to down one cent. The East/West spread narrowed by 3.6 cents to 22.9 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 70 lots traded, down from Thursday's 158.
